evidence.scope: doctor gains one check: a ticket's frontmatter status must agree with its own journal, and where it does not, doctor says so and repairs nothing.
acceptance: A ticket whose journal ends in a receipt whose commit is merged, but whose status is not done, is reported with both values: evidenced by a test and by the two real cases that prompted the ticket
A ticket at a working stage whose status says done or todo is reported: evidenced by a test for each
SEEN-086 passes: done, no journal, exempt as the bootstrap and recorded as such in CLAUDE.md: evidenced by doctor on this tree
A delivered ticket whose receipt is not yet merged and whose status is review passes: evidenced by a test, because that is the normal state between delivery and merge
doctor repairs nothing: evidenced by a test asserting the wrong status is still there afterwards
decisions: The check compares four things and nothing more: the frontmatter status, the journal's last record, whether the receipt's commit is merged, and the bootstrap exemption. Anything richer would need judgement, and doctor reports facts
Merged means the receipt's commit is an ancestor of the default branch, the same test reopen already uses, so the two cannot disagree about what merged means

A ticket with no journal and no receipt is only exempt when it is SEEN-086: the exemption is named rather than inferred from the absence of a journal, because every unstarted ticket also has no journal
An unstarted ticket, status todo with no journal, is not reported: that is the normal state of 80 tickets and a check that reports it would be noise
graph_impact: doctor already walks every journal and every ticket file, so the check has both halves in hand
